description: The Living Lab at the University of Salford is a retrofit demonstration of integrated nature-based solutions, a green-blue roof, a 185 m living wall, sustainable drainage tree pits and a rain garden, all connected to one central real-time monitoring system that also redistributes rainwater. It was central to IGNITION, a Greater Manchester project from 2019 building the case for urban nature-based solutions, and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority reports its findings on GM Green City. Coverage is one university site in Salford. Findings include about 6 degrees difference in building envelope temperature where the green wall stands, SuDS with 70,000 litres of capacity capturing surface water from an area ten times the lab footprint, and a wall of over 5,800 plants of more than 50 species. Format and access: a web article; monitoring data are not published. Licence: not stated; free to read. Caveats: the results are summaries from the project, not a peer-reviewed data set. It gives evidence for climate adaptation planning with green infrastructure. Related catalogue records are Salford City Council greenspace data and the NGIF sensor data set.
